simple.meaning: מְקֵרָה (mᵉqêrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a cooling off.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מְקֵרָה (H4747) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 3:20, with occurrences in Judges.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְקֵרָה (H4747) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מְקֵרָה (H4747) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מְקֵרָה (mᵉqêrâh) / H4747 is traced through Judges 3:20, Judges 3:24 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.

timeline.evidenceText: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
After he had gone, his servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, “Surely he is covering his feet† or, “relieving himself”. in the upper room.”
